subtitle: Cross-Sovereign Mutual Appeal, Consent Revocation, Effect Fencing, and Remedy Extension

new_primitives.SOVEREIGN_DOMAIN_ID: Identifier for an independently governed domain whose internal finality does not automatically bind a peer domain.
new_primitives.INTERFACE_COVENANT_ID: Identifier for a provenance-bound agreement governing a defined interaction between sovereign domains without merging them.
new_primitives.CONSENT_SCOPE_ID: Identifier binding permission to subject, action/effect class, purpose, scope, version, time and revocation semantics.
new_primitives.CONSENT_REVOCATION_RECEIPT: Record proving a revocation event, acknowledgement state and transition to a new authority epoch.
new_primitives.AUTHORITY_EPOCH: Monotonic interaction-authority version used to reject stale permissions at a final pre-effect fence.
new_primitives.CROSS_SOVEREIGN_APPEAL_ID: Identifier for a dispute that carries local review receipts from more than one sovereign domain.
new_primitives.MUTUAL_REVIEW_RECEIPT: Record of the two local conclusions, shared interface rules, unresolved conflicts and any preagreed forum disposition.
new_primitives.NEUTRAL_FORUM_PROFILE_ID: Precommitted shared review profile whose authority is limited to an explicitly admitted interface scope.
new_primitives.REMEDY_RECEIPT: Record linking an unauthorized or invalidated effect to mitigation, restoration, correction, reliance repair, notice or unresolved remedy status.

core_rule: Internal finality ends at the sovereign-domain boundary. A materially affecting act must carry current interface authority at the last meaningful pre-effect fence, and acknowledged revocation invalidates stale consent for future revocable effects without erasing prior history or validly incurred obligations.
authority_pipeline: INTERNAL_ADMISSIBILITY -> EXTERNAL_EFFECT_CLASSIFICATION -> CURRENT_INTERFACE_AUTHORITY_EPOCH_CHECK -> COMMIT|BLOCK|HOLD -> EFFECT_RECEIPT -> APPEAL_IF_CHALLENGED -> MUTUAL_REVIEW -> UPHOLD|BLOCK|REMEDY_REQUIRED|SHARED_FORUM_REVIEW|CROSS_SOVEREIGN_CONFLICT_UNRESOLVED

consent_revocation_rule.grant: Consent creates only the explicitly scoped permission described by its receipt.
consent_revocation_rule.revocation: Acknowledged revocation transitions relevant future revocable effects to a new authority epoch.

remedy_rule.anti_laundering: A remedy cannot rewrite the original event as authorized or retroactively consented.

neutral_forum_rule: A shared forum may bind the interaction only when both domains admitted its identity, scope and rule version before the dispute or through a new mutually accepted agreement; forum authority cannot silently expand into either domain's internal identity.
verification_requirements: two peer domains reject reciprocal self-supremacy claims
revoked consent is rejected at the last pre-effect authority fence
consent revocation does not erase a distinct prior obligation ledger
in-flight stale authority is cancelled where possible or opens remedy if effect already occurs
incompatible local appellate outcomes return CROSS_SOVEREIGN_CONFLICT_UNRESOLVED when no shared final forum exists
preagreed neutral forum works only inside its admitted scope
remedy preserves original effect and authority timeline
emergency exception cannot be invented after revocation
external appeal cannot capture either domain's internal identity
canonical_lines: Two sovereign domains can share an interface without sharing a throne.
Consent is current authority only inside its scope and epoch; an acknowledged revocation makes the old permission stale.
Revocation changes what may happen next; it does not delete what already happened.
A remedy repairs an unauthorized effect without rewriting it as authorized.
When two internal courts disagree, neither becomes the court of the world merely by calling itself final.
claim_ceiling: Technical specification candidate only; no executable consent/revocation engine, legal doctrine, production cross-domain arbitration, formal proof, or independent implementation replay is claimed.
